Specific projective-object morphic dyads automatically correspond to English object personal pronouns.
+c-Ø( can realize the specific third-person common-or-singular projective object pronoun.
+qu-Ø( can realize the specific third-person common-or-singular projective object pronoun.
+qui-Ø( can realize the specific third-person common-or-singular projective object pronoun.
With a singular human male object, +c-Ø( / +qu-Ø( ~ +qui-Ø( can be rendered ‘him.’
With a singular human female object, +c-Ø( / +qu-Ø( ~ +qui-Ø( can be rendered ‘her.’
With a singular animate nonhuman object, +c-Ø( / +qu-Ø( ~ +qui-Ø( can be rendered ‘it.’
With a singular nonanimate object, +c-Ø( / +qu-Ø( ~ +qui-Ø( can be rendered ‘it.’
With plural nonanimate objects, common-number +c-Ø( / +qu-Ø( ~ +qui-Ø( can be rendered ‘them.’
+qu-im( realizes a specific third-person plural animate projective-object pronoun.
With plural human objects, +qu-im( can be rendered ‘them.’
With plural animate nonhuman objects, +qu-im( can be rendered ‘them.’
All phonologically conditioned assimilated variants of +qu-im( are included as grammatical realizations of the same plural animate object pronoun.
In a mainline reflexive-object construction, subposition va1 carries number information.
The va1 filler n realizes first-person singular in a mainline reflexive-object construction.
The va1 filler t realizes first-person plural in a mainline reflexive-object construction.
Each mainline reflexive-object morphic dyad in the §6.7 paradigm realizes its indicated person-number value.
With a second-person singular human subject, +m-o( ~ +m-⎕( has the reflexive object value ‘yourself.’
With a third-person singular male-human subject, the nonfirst reflexive object has the value ‘himself.’
With a third-person singular female-human subject, the nonfirst reflexive object has the value ‘herself.’
With a third-person singular nonhuman subject, the nonfirst reflexive object has the value ‘itself.’
With a second-person plural human subject, the nonfirst reflexive object can have the reflexive value ‘yourselves.’
With a second-person plural human subject, the same morph can have the reciprocal value ‘one another.’
With a third-person plural subject, the nonfirst reflexive object can have the reflexive value ‘themselves.’
With a third-person plural subject, the same morph can have the reciprocal value ‘one another.’
Reciprocal ‘one another’ is licensed only with a plural subject interpretation, whereas singular subjects receive reflexive readings.
